subject: Hosted API — data residency, erasure assurances and backup policy
messages:
From: Ellen Dawson <ellen.dawson@stratushealth.com>

Cc: security@stratushealth.com

Subject: Hosted API — data residency / erasure questions

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security & privacy team has a short set of follow-ups specific to the hosted API. Can you confirm the following for Stratus Health (PHI-adjacent workload)?

1) Where live customer request data and model context are stored geographically (primary and any replicas)?
2) What backup/snapshot cadence and retention windows apply to hosted API customer data and system snapshots?
3) If we request a full tenant erasure, what is the end-to-end timeline and what systems retain residual copies (snapshots, object storage backups, monitoring/metrics)?
4) Do you offer an expedited erasure option (shorter backup retention) in contract? If so, what are the operational steps?
5) What evidence/artifacts will you provide to prove deletion?

We appreciate concise, actionable answers. If it's easier to provide a short attestation pack we can accept that as well.

Best,
Ellen Dawson
Head of Security Programs
Stratus Health

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Dawson <ellen.dawson@stratushealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2027 02:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API — data residency / erasure questions

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear list. Answers below at a high level; attaching a short evidence pack and our deletion flow diagram. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to walk through.

1) Geography / replication:
- Primary storage: us-west-2 (AWS) for Stratus Health by default.
- Replication: asynchronous cross-AZ replication within us-west-2; cross-region replication to us-east-1 for DR only (no EU or APAC replicas for US-tenanted accounts unless explicitly contracted).

2) Backups / snapshots:
- Live object/state snapshots: automated snapshots every 6 hours, retained for 7 days by default.
- Long-term backups: daily backups captured and retained in encrypted object storage for 30 days.
- Immutable archival backups (cold) retained for up to 90 days for disaster recovery and legal hold processing, encrypted with customer-segregated CMKs for enterprise customers.

3) Tenant erasure timeline & residual systems:
- On receipt of a verified erasure request (ticket + authorized admin), primary records are deleted from the live datastores within 24 hours.
- Background purge jobs scrub indexes and metadata within 72 hours.
- Backups and snapshots: standard hosted path means backups may persist for up to 90 days — these are encrypted and stored separately; restoration to recover deleted data is protected by access controls and is treated as a security event if attempted.
- Monitoring/metrics/analytics: aggregated telemetry is pseudonymized and retained for 90 days; raw request payloads are not included in analytics by default.

4) Expedited erasure option:
- Yes, for enterprise deals we can offer an expedited erase addendum (contractual) that reduces standard backup retention to 30 days and triggers accelerated lifecycle policies on the storage tier. Operational steps: sign addendum -> open erasure request -> we execute standard erasure flow -> we run expedited purge on backups and provide attestation. This is available for hosted customers under an addendum and for Dedicated/Private we can do more aggressive physical deletion.

5) Evidence / artifacts provided:
- Deletion manifest (GUIDs, object keys removed)
- Audit log extract showing deletion events and operator IDs
- Signed attestation PDF (optional)

Attachments: deletion_process_diagram.pdf, backup_retention_matrix.csv, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

If you need tighter windows (e.g., <30 days) we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment where we can provide stronger guarantees and physical control.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2027 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API — data residency / erasure questions

Hi Ellen — copying in a couple of specifics from Security & Compliance.

A) Backup retention and contractual options:
- The 90-day archival is our default DR posture for hosted accounts to support recovery and industry-standard legal holds. It is not immutable: we can include an expedited retention clause in the enterprise addendum that reduces archival retention to 30 days for the affected tenant. That clause spells out the tradeoffs (recovery window reduced, and certain disaster scenarios may not be recoverable).

B) KV caches & logs:
- KV caches are in-memory first; short-lived cache shards are not written to persistent backups in normal operation. Transient cache checkpoints (for warm-start recovery) are excluded from long-term backups; they have TTLs measured in minutes/hours.
- Request traces and full request payloads: by default, we capture request metadata and an event-level trace for debugging which excludes full prompt/response payloads unless debugging mode is enabled by the customer. Full request payloads are not written to backups or cold archives in normal operations. Logs that contain payload excerpts are redacted and stored only for 30 days in the default hosted config.

C) Evidence and attestation workflow:
- We produce a deletion manifest and export of audit logs for the erasure transaction. For procurement, we can provide a signed attestation PDF and a Drive folder with the manifest and redaction-safe screenshots of the audit timeline.

Attached: expedited_erase_addendum_template.docx

If you want, Kimberly from Sales can scope the addendum and provide estimated pricing/acceptance language for procurement.

— Irene Choi
